Counsel for Applicant :- Sandeep Kumar Rai Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
1-Mr. Manoj Kumar Srivastava, learned Advocate, filed his power/Vakalatnama on behalf of opposite party no.2, which is taken on record.

2-Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State of U.P./opposite party no.1,
learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 and perused and record.

3-The instant application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been preferred by the applicant to quash the charge sheet dated 08.10.2018, cognizance/ summoning order dated 02.11.2018 and proceeding of Special Session Trial No. 738 of 2018 (State versus Rajan Chaudhary) arising out of Case Crime No. 440 of 2016, under Sections, 376, 511, 452 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station-Pipraich, District-Gorakhpur, pending in the Court of Special Judge, POCSO Court No.4,
Rajan Chaudhary vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189772015/
1 Gorakhpur.
4-The main substratum of argument of learned counsel for the applicant is that in this case F.I.R.
was lodged after one month and twenty-three days on 20.09.2016 with regard to an incident dated 27.07.2016.

sentences.text: After submission of charge sheet, the informant and the victim have been examined before the trial Court as PW-1 and PW-2 on 18.04.2022 and 26.04.2022 respectively, but on account of compromise between the parties, they have not supported the prosecution case and have been declared hostile by the trial Court at the request of the prosecution.

It is also submitted that from the statement of PW-1 and PW-2, the offence under Section 376 I.P.C. is not made out and the informant as well as the victim do not want to continue the criminal proceeding against the applicant, therefore, the same may be quashed.

5-The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the opposite party no.2 also submits that now the parties concerned have settled their dispute, therefore, the informant and the victim have no grievance against the applicant, in case, criminal proceeding against him is quashed by this Court.

6-However, learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the aforesaid contention made by the learned counsel for the applicant by contending that in view of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Laxmi Narayan and others, (2019) 5 SCC 688, the parties concerned cannot be permitted to make compromise in an offence of rape, which is an offence against the society at large.
7-Having heard the submission of learned counsel for the parties and perused the record, I find substance in the submission of learned A.G.A. that in view of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Laxmi Narayan and others (Supra), the criminal prosecution of the applicant with regard to an offence of rape and the offence under POCSO Act cannot be quashed on the basis of compromise.

entities.text: State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Laxmi Narayan and others, (2019) 5 SCC 688
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Laxmi Narayan and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
So far as charge is concerned, the same can be altered at any time by the trial Court before the judgment is pronounced in view of Section 216 Cr.P.C.
8-In view of the above, the relief as sought by the applicant through the instant application is hereby refused.
9-This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. lacks merit and is, accordingly, dismissed.
